source: Keeping Judgment Load-Bearing — 28 proposals for teams where most code is written by a model
note: Proposals, not measured results. Each entry is pilotable on one team for one quarter with the success metric declared in advance.

products.name: Comprehension debt ledger
products.what: A last-explained-by field per module, set only when a human reconstructs that module's behaviour at a whiteboard without reading it. Dashboard the share of production code no current employee can explain.
products.why: Technical debt has a ledger, a review and an owner. Understanding decays just as fast and has none of the three.

products.name: Prediction-first review
products.what: Before opening an AI-written diff the reviewer writes three predictions: where the bug is, what is over-engineered, which test is missing. Then they read. Scores compared monthly.
products.why: Passive review of plausible code builds no pattern library. A forced prediction turns the same thirty minutes into calibration training at zero infrastructure cost.

products.name: Trust-calibration scoreboards
products.what: On every accepted suggestion the developer logs a one-click confidence: will this need a fix within thirty days? Join against the next thirty days of commits and incidents to get a calibration curve per person.
products.why: Knowing when to distrust the model is the central skill of this era and nobody measures it. Everyone measures acceptance rate, which is the wrong number.

products.name: Cold rebuild drills
products.what: Monthly, a developer re-derives an AI-written module from its spec and tests alone, never seeing the code, then diffs their version against production.
products.why: It measures whether comprehension kept pace with throughput — the one thing velocity dashboards cannot see.

products.name: A manual load-bearing core
products.what: Name the 5-10% of the system where shallow understanding is catastrophic: money movement, auth, concurrency, migrations, idempotency and retries. The model may propose there; a human types.
products.why: Not purity — cost-weighted. The blast radius of not understanding a payment path is nothing like that of a settings page.
products.implementedBy: tier (partially: tier computes the core from telemetry instead of naming it by hand)

products.name: Bug-injection gym on your own repo
products.what: Wire mutation testing into a timed exercise where developers hunt injected defects in real company code, scored on time to find and on false positives.
products.why: Puzzle-site practice transfers to interviews. Hunting mutants in code you own transfers to Tuesday.

products.name: The reverse rubber duck
products.what: The author explains the change to an agent configured as a relentless skeptical junior that only asks questions. The transcript attaches to the pull request.
products.why: It turns understanding into a reviewable artifact — a reviewer can see whether the author could answer "what happens on the second retry" before merging.

products.name: Invert the junior and the model
products.what: The junior writes the first draft, the model critiques it, the senior reviews the critique.
products.why: The default arrangement is the worst possible allocation of the learning. Generation practice belongs with the person who still needs to build it.

products.name: A deliberate-difficulty budget
products.what: A set number of hours each week per developer of explicitly model-free work above their current level, tracked as a first-class commitment.
products.why: Training load is managed deliberately in every field where capability decays under comfort. Software assumed capability maintains itself.

products.name: Code club
products.what: Weekly, like a journal club: one AI-written module read aloud and critiqued, juniors reading and seniors arguing.
products.why: Juniors learned by reading seniors' code. Seniors do not write much any more, so that apprenticeship channel closed without anyone deciding to close it.

products.name: A house taste corpus
products.what: Not a style guide — a curated set of real good and bad examples from your own repository, each with the reason attached. Developers classify fresh samples blind, then see the house answer.
products.why: Taste cannot be prompted for and is learned from examples, not rules. The corpus doubles as retrieval context for your agents.

products.name: Hire and promote on diagnosis, not authoring
products.what: Interview against a broken running system with AI fully allowed, scored on hypothesis quality, instrumentation choices and time to correct diagnosis.
products.why: What an organisation selects for is what it preserves. Authoring is being automated; diagnosis is being left behind.

products.name: Mandatory "why not the alternative"
products.what: One paragraph with every AI-produced design naming the rejected option and the cost of choosing this one. Harvested automatically into decision records.
products.why: Models generate plausible architecture with no trade-off reasoning attached, so the reasoning is never written down — and that is what the next maintainer needs.

products.name: Regeneration as a spec-tightness metric
products.what: Re-generate a component from its specification with a different model and seed, then differential-test old and new against replayed production traffic. Divergence names the underspecified clause.
products.why: Specifications are normally aspirational prose. Regeneration makes them falsifiable and gives spec quality a score.

products.name: Incident-to-eval pipeline
products.what: Every production incident becomes a permanent eval case in your agent harness: would the current agent, with the current context, have written this bug? Run the corpus on every model, prompt and rule change.
products.why: Teams regression-test their application rigorously and upgrade the thing writing it blind. Your outage history is the highest-signal eval set you will ever have and it is already written down.

products.name: Canary the coding agent like a production dependency
products.what: Shadow-run a candidate model over last month's merged pull requests and compare tests passed, review churn and diff size. Pin versions, roll out behind a flag, keep a rollback path.
products.why: A model upgrade currently lands on every engineer at once with no validation — a dependency bump with org-wide blast radius and none of the controls you would demand of a library.

products.name: A context compiler with its own CI
products.what: Compile decision records, incidents, deprecations, ownership and settled decisions into a versioned context artifact for agents — then lint it. Fail the build on contradictory rules, stale rules and rules no agent has retrieved in ninety days.
products.why: Enterprise AI failure is overwhelmingly a context-operations problem rather than a model problem, and context is the one input in the pipeline with no owner, no tests and no expiry.

products.name: Agent friction as a developer-experience metric
products.what: Log where agents repeatedly stall, retry or thrash in your repository. Rank platform investment by agent-hours lost per module.
products.why: The places a model gets stuck are the places humans get stuck, and the model produces a clean, high-volume, unembarrassed signal about it. Buildable in a week from logs you already keep.

products.name: Swarm and select for migrations
products.what: Run the same migration several times over in isolated worktrees with different agents and approaches. Select on test outcomes plus sampled human review. Discard the rest without sentiment.
products.why: Treats generation as a search with a selection step instead of one attempt to be laboriously corrected. The economics only started working recently.

products.name: Risk-tiered autonomy computed from your own telemetry
products.what: Derive autonomy level per change from blast radius, test coverage of the touched paths, the file's incident history and reversibility. Well-covered leaf code: cheap model, auto-merge. Payment path: strongest model, two humans, dual-key on anything irreversible.
products.why: Most organisations set one global policy for all code, which is simultaneously too slow for the trivial ninety percent and far too loose for the dangerous one percent.

products.name: Oracle isolation
products.what: The test-writing agent never sees the implementation; the implementing agent never sees the tests until CI. Enforced by tooling, not policy.
products.why: It structurally kills the dominant agent failure mode — tests written to assert the behaviour of the bug — which review catches late and often not at all.

products.name: A pre-mortem agent in design review
products.what: An agent grounded in your incident corpus reviews each design document and names the three most likely ways it fails in production, citing the outages it is reasoning from.
products.why: Institutional memory as a standing reviewer. The people who remember the 2019 outage have left; the postmortem is still on the wiki, unread.

products.name: Spec excavation before legacy rewrites
products.what: Point agents at the legacy service plus its real production traffic and have them produce a characterisation test suite and an inferred specification first. Only then start the rewrite, with an executable definition of "same behaviour".
products.why: Rewrites fail because nobody knows what the old system does. Highest-value item here for most large organisations and the one with a direct budget case.

products.name: An entropy agent with a deletion target
products.what: An always-on agent whose only measured output is net lines deleted, dead code removed and duplicated logic collapsed, with the suite green and a human approving each batch.
products.why: Generation drives code volume up relentlessly and nobody is staffed on the other direction. Also the safest agent to run: every change is a subtraction and the tests are the contract.

products.name: Behaviour diff, and planning against review capacity
products.what: Every pull request carries a generated behaviour delta in plain language, a risk map, and the agent's own note on where it would look for bugs. Then plan sprints against review bandwidth with a WIP limit on open agent pull requests.
products.why: The bottleneck moved from writing to reviewing and planning practice has not moved with it. Queues form at the new constraint whether or not anyone models it.

products.name: An eval-gated internal skill marketplace
products.what: Teams publish prompts, skills and subagents; promotion to an org-wide default requires passing a shared eval suite. Owners, versions, service levels and a deprecation path, as for an internal library.
products.why: Prompt and agent sprawl is the next shadow IT: hundreds of unversioned, unowned, undocumented behaviours already running against production repositories.

products.name: Continuous audit evidence
products.what: Agents map each change to the control requirements it touches and emit audit evidence as a by-product of CI rather than a quarterly archaeology project.
products.why: Regulated organisations burn enormous senior-engineer time reassembling, after the fact, a story the pipeline already knew at the time.

products.name: Counterfactual postmortems
products.what: After each incident, replay it against the current agent and context: would this have been caught? If not, what context was missing? Feed that answer back into the context compiler.
products.why: It closes the loop between production reality and agent capability, which otherwise drift apart silently for as long as nobody checks.
